## Plan document present and linked

Pass. The planning issue requires `dev/active/9b7b5f9c-plan.md` ([issue record](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b7b5f9c/.jit/issues/ca024a2b-561d-432c-99f0-3a9ded3451d5.json:4)); the document exists, is substantive, and is linked as a design document at line 134. All three linked local documents were reviewed in full. The planning issue has no dependencies.

## Completeness against criteria

Pass. The plan explicitly addresses all twelve hard criteria in its coverage table ([plan](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b7b5f9c/dev/active/9b7b5f9c-plan.md:5)) and carries each into concrete leaf criteria and the decomposition coverage map at line 138.

The exclusions at line 22 match the authoritative post-1.0 deferrals in the [MVP scope brief](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b7b5f9c/dev/active/9b7b5f9c-mvp-scope-brief.md:28); no required MVP scope is silently narrowed.

## Technical soundness and architectural fit

Pass. The domain/storage/command/CLI split at plan line 26 matches the repository architecture. Its claims about current behavior are accurate:

- Initialization currently mutates incrementally after constructing storage and the executor ([main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b7b5f9c/crates/jit/src/main.rs:1703)).
- Repository discovery currently ignores partial `.jit` directories, explaining why pre-validation recovery needs separate discovery ([discovery.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b7b5f9c/crates/jit/src/storage/discovery.rs:33)).
- The server validates storage before constructing its executor, so startup recovery must precede that validation ([server main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b7b5f9c/crates/server/src/main.rs:61)).
- Event append is independently fallible, supporting the decision to publish the next event-log image transactionally ([json.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b7b5f9c/crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:828)).

The manifest, overlay-validation, capability-confined publication, event consistency, and recovery-boundary designs are sufficiently concrete and preserve the domain-agnostic invariant.

## Decomposition and dependencies

Pass. The twelve leaves form a coherent, acyclic, transitively reduced sequence:

`manifest + overlay + transaction + checkers → planner/recovery/projection → application → payload → public commands → documentation → end-to-end acceptance`

Each leaf has an outcome, owned hard criteria, blast radius, gates, dependencies, and green landing. The production payload is correctly delayed until generic package, transaction, checker, and projection mechanics exist; public exposure follows the complete payload; cross-platform acceptance closes the graph without absorbing component-level test ownership.

## Risks and actionability

Pass. The critical risks at plan lines 159–177 have concrete decisions or mitigations, including journal placement, recovery timing, event consistency, symlink races, source-of-truth drift, placeholder-review visibility, and platform-specific mode semantics. Decisions D1–D12 resolve the load-bearing choices sufficiently for breakdown and implementation.

## Prior review feedback

Pass. All three prior blockers are resolved:

- F1: Projection configuration is now represented as complete singleton-table manifest contributions (plan line 27), with production acceptance at line 117.
- F2: Fresh-root recovery state now lives outside `.jit/` in `.jit-bootstrap/` (lines 31 and 69–74).
- F3: Recovery now runs before storage validation and repository-dependent cache construction for CLI and server entry points (lines 34 and 76–81).

## Findings

No findings.
